national-city-christian-church-dc.assessment: National City Christian Church is the architectural and ecclesiastical "cathedral" of the Christian Church (Disciples of Christ) — a neoclassical John Russell Pope landmark on Thomas Circle, completed 1930, with stained-glass windows commemorating Presidents James A. Garfield and Lyndon B. Johnson, both Disciples. President Johnson occasionally attended during his presidency and his state funeral was held here on January 25, 1973. The church called The Rev. Stephanie Kendell as its first female senior pastor and president in 2023 — she previously served as 1st Vice-Moderator of the entire denomination. Disciples of Christ as a whole is mainline-progressive: non-inerrantist, egalitarian, with many Open & Affirming congregations and openly affirming LGBT clergy. NCCC publicly aligns with this trajectory. By MOOP's rubric the church is red across gender, cultural, denominational, and preaching dimensions — beautiful building, beautiful presidential history, theological distance significant.

national-community-church-dc.assessment: National Community Church under Mark Batterson is culturally influential, evangelistically aggressive, and Batterson himself is clearly Christ-centered in his books and preaching. NCC is known for meeting in movie theaters, Ebenezers Coffeehouse (their ministry-owned coffee shop), and reaching young professionals in DC. The Assemblies of God affiliation provides structure and accountability. However: AoG's charismatic framework, Batterson's topical preaching style, and the DC-area cultural pressure points are real concerns for a man wanting deep doctrinal formation. Visit with discernment. NCC is a good entry point for unchurched people and city engagement, but may not be the primary spiritual food source for a man wanting expository depth.

score_notes.scripture: Assemblies of God affirms Scripture inerrancy, but charismatic framework adds extra-biblical 'words of knowledge,' prophecy, and experience-driven spirituality that can compete with Scripture's authority.
score_notes.gender: Assemblies of God historically has allowed women in pastoral roles. NCC's stance on female senior pastors/elders needs individual verification — Batterson is complementarian but AoG doesn't require it.
score_notes.soteriology: AoG affirms faith alone for salvation (sola fide), but may add 'second blessing' / baptism of the Holy Spirit with tongues as normative expectation. Salvation clearly gospel-centered but framework can add layers.
score_notes.preaching: Batterson is a gifted communicator and visionary thinker. However, his style is more topical/narrative than expository. He's an ideas guy and cultural connector, not a verse-by-verse expositor.
score_notes.cultural: NCC operates in the DC political ecosystem and intentionally engages culture — both a strength (marketplace presence) and risk (drift). Language around 'justice' should be evaluated. | MOOP-attendance note: Adam Johns attended NCC many years ago. Historical attendance only — does not extend to current-trajectory endorsement (NCC remains RED-rated for charismatic/Bathersonian "your dream is what God wants" framing per existing assessment). | CONSOLIDATION 2026-04-28: Three duplicate records existed (national-community-church-dc, -dc-2, -dc-3). Merged to this canonical record. Rating elevated from RED to BLACK based on prior dc-2 framing: "Assemblies of God multi-site, Mark Batterson, Revoice-adjacent." NCC has been linked to Side B sympathetic content, prosperity-adjacent "your dream is what God wants" theology, and post-2020 cultural-conformity drift. Adam (MOOP) attended NCC many years ago — historical attendance flagged but does not extend to current-trajectory endorsement.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: NCC has life groups and men's engagement, but no dedicated men's discipleship infrastructure as the primary vehicle.
score_notes.denominational: Assemblies of God — provides accountability, but AoG's charismatic framework introduces tensions around gender roles and extra-biblical spiritual gifts.
score_notes.christology: Assemblies of God affiliation affirms Trinity and Christ's deity per AG Fundamental Truths. NCC homepage does not articulate doctrine specifically; generic Jesus-focused language. Green on denominational default.
score_notes.leadership: Lead Pastor Mark Batterson with Pastor Joel Schmidgall and team; AG affirms women in pastoral ministry (NCC has had female teaching pastors). Single-charismatic-leader-plus-team model — watch for celebrity-pastor dynamic.
score_notes.mission: Mission: 'Bless the Lord. Bless the City. Bless the Nations. Bless the Generations.' — Great Commission framed with 'launching pad for world-changers' language emphasizing cultural influence.

national-community-church-dc.gender_detail: AoG allows women in ministry roles — NCC's specific elder/pastoral gender policy needs verification; Batterson is personally complementarian but AoG denominational policy allows female ordination

national-presbyterian-church-dc.assessment: National Presbyterian Church occupies a historic building with its cornerstone laid by President Eisenhower and has served Washington DC's elite for generations. However, as a PCUSA congregation, it operates within a denomination that has formally abandoned biblical standards on human sexuality (same-sex marriage and LGBTQ+ ordination approved 2015), Scripture authority, and gender roles. For USMC Ministries purposes: the PCUSA is not a theologically safe harbor for Gospel-grounded men. This church is listed because it is nationally prominent and Washington DC visitors will encounter it — but the rating is red. Men seeking Reformed Presbyterian theology in DC should look to PCA or EPC congregations instead. Note: the building is stunning and historically significant — Moop may encounter this church in civic contexts.
